awd_titl_txt: STTR Phase I: Fibroblast-Derived Engineered Extracellular Vesicles (eEVs) as New Nucleic Acid Therapeutic Delivery Systems for Peripheral Nervous System (PNS) Genetic Disorders
awd_abstract_narration:
The broader impact/commercial potential of this Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Phase I project lies in its ability to advance gene therapy for neurological disorders by developing a scalable and cost-effective manufacturing process for extracellular vesicle (EV)-based therapeutics. This innovation has the potential to improve treatment safety, precision, and accessibility for patients with conditions such as neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), addressing a critical unmet medical need. By streamlining production methods, this project aims to lower the cost of EV-based therapies, making them more widely available. Additionally, the technology is expected to drive growth in the U.S. biotechnology sector, fostering job creation and reinforcing the nation's leadership in gene therapy innovation. The commercial potential is significant, as this approach may enable the development of novel, non-viral gene therapies with broad applications in precision medicine.

This Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Phase I project seeks to address key technical challenges in the scalable manufacturing of EV-based gene therapies. The research focuses on improving methods for EV isolation, purification, and cargo loading to enhance therapeutic efficacy. Specific objectives include optimizing culture conditions, refining chemical transfection protocols, and developing standardized procedures for loading exogenous DNA into EVs. The project will also evaluate biodistribution, dosing, and therapeutic outcomes in preclinical models to support future clinical translation. Anticipated technical results include the establishment of reproducible, scalable manufacturing protocols and the demonstration of in vitro efficacy. This work will contribute to the broader field of precision medicine by providing an alternative to viral vectors for gene delivery, addressing current limitations in safety, scalability, and immune response.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

Project Title: STTR Phase I: Fibroblast-Derived Engineered Extracellular Vesicles (eEVs) as New Nucleic Acid Therapeutic Delivery Systems for Peripheral Nervous System (PNS) Genetic Disorders
Awardee Organization: Neucore Bio, Inc. | Award Number (FAIN): 2507437 | Principal Investigator: Silvia Duarte-Sanmiguel, Ph.D.

Peripheral Nervous System (PNS) genetic disorders, such as Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1), affect tens of thousands of children and adults across the United States. These conditions cause severe, lifelong disabilities, chronic pain, and debilitating nerve tumors known as neurofibromas. Although advanced gene therapies offer the potential to address the underlying genetic causes of these diseases, current delivery tools face major clinical hurdles. In particular, conventional viral delivery vectors (such as adeno-associated viruses) cannot carry large therapeutic genes like the NF1 gene, which exceeds standard packaging limits. Furthermore, viral delivery carries risks of toxic immune reactions, cannot be safely re-administered, and lacks natural precision targeting for peripheral nerve cells.

To overcome these fundamental barriers, Neucore Bio, Inc., in close collaboration with researchers at The Ohio State University, has developed a breakthrough non-viral biological delivery platform known as FixE. This innovative technology harnesses extracellular vesicles (EVs)—nanoscale biological messengers naturally produced by human cells. By transiently reprogramming abundant, accessible skin cells (human dermal fibroblasts) toward a nerve-supporting Schwann cell identity, Neucore Bio produces engineered extracellular vesicles that inherently display natural biological homing signals targeting diseased peripheral nerve cells, eliminating the need for complex and costly synthetic chemical modifications.

With support from this National Science Foundation Phase I STTR award (Award #2507437), Neucore Bio achieved several foundational technical milestones:

1. Scalable Manufacturing & Culture Media Optimization: Working with commercial bioprocessing standards, the team established chemically defined culture media formulations that doubled extracellular vesicle production yields (>2-fold increase) while completely eliminating bovine serum contaminants, establishing a direct path toward large-scale bioreactor manufacturing.

2. Post-Isolation Cargo Packaging: The team pioneered and validated scalable, non-cell-based methods to package large genetic payloads (both plasmid DNA and messenger RNA) into purified vesicles post-harvest, achieving high encapsulation efficiency while preserving nanoscale vesicle stability.

3. Target Tropism, Intracellular Delivery & Molecular Rescue: In rigorous cell culture trials using patient-derived NF1-deficient Schwann cells, the team demonstrated that engineered vesicles selectively target and enter diseased Schwann cells. Importantly, systematic comparisons between culture formulations identified key trade-offs between manufacturing yield and biological targeting potency, establishing the exact roadmap for refined clinical formulations. Delivered therapeutic genetic cargos successfully escaped endosomal compartments, underwent functional protein translation, and triggered comprehensive normalization of critical disease pathways—restoring healthy tumor-suppressor controls, re-establishing proper cell death checkpoints, and suppressing chronic inflammatory signaling.

4. Commercial De-Risking, Clinical Partnerships & Patient-Centered Strategy: In parallel with laboratory technical milestones, Neucore Bio's executive leadership completed the national NSF Innovation Corps (I-Corps) customer discovery program. The team formally defined the clinical Target Product Profile (TPP) for FixE-NF1, established Plexiform Neurofibromas as the lead clinical program, and engaged directly with NF1 patients, families, and clinicians. This initiative established vital relationships with premier disease advocacy organizations, including the Children's Tumor Foundation (CTF) and the Gilbert Family Foundation, alongside leading clinical experts such as Dr. D. Wade Clapp at Indiana University School of Medicine, aligning our non-viral genetic therapeutic pipeline directly with clinical adoption pathways.

The successful completion of this Phase I project establishes the technical feasibility of engineered extracellular vesicles as targeted, high-capacity non-viral delivery vehicles for large genetic medicines. Beyond Neurofibromatosis, the FixE platform offers a modular, re-administrable delivery solution for a wide range of currently intractable peripheral nerve disorders, including Charcot-Marie-Tooth neuropathies. These results establish the technological and commercial foundation for Phase II development, during which Neucore Bio will transfer the validated manufacturing protocol to commercial CDMO Lonza and execute in vivo preclinical trials in gold-standard disease models at Indiana University School of Medicine, bringing curative non-viral gene therapies closer to patients in need.
